draft.title: Shoguns, daimyo and samurai
card: Emperor
the emperor lived in the capital and was treated with respect, but had little real power in feudal Japan.
Shogun
the military leader who actually ruled Japan. He held the most power, and a shogun's family could pass the title on.
Daimyo
powerful lords who held large areas of land. They ruled their own lands and supported the shogun.
Samurai
warriors who served a daimyo. They fought for their lord and were given a place of high rank in society.
draft.remember: The shogun ruled, daimyo held the land, and samurai served the daimyo.

a.q: Who held the real power to rule Japan in feudal times?
opts: The emperor, who lived in the capital
A samurai, a lord of the land
a.why: The shogun was the military leader who ruled Japan. The emperor was respected but had little real power, which makes him the most tempting wrong answer.
a.clue: Think about who led the army and ruled, not who was honoured.

b.q: Lord Takeda held a large area of land in Japan and had warriors who fought for him. What was his role?
b.why: A daimyo was a lord who held land and had samurai serving him. A samurai is wrong because samurai were the warriors, not the lord who held the land.
b.clue: Who holds the land, and who serves him?

problems.detail: Two distractors attach wrong descriptions to the roles ('A samurai, a lord of the land' and 'A daimyo, a samurai warrior'). They could teach students the wrong pairings, and they muddle the hierarchy the card sets out. They also leave the shogun as the only option whose description matches the card, so a student could pick it by matching descriptions.
